subject: Renewal: flexible buffer, overage handling and tiered step-down model
messages:
From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acme-analytics.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal planning — right-sizing + overage / buffer options

Hi Soojin,

Hope you’re well. Our renewal for the hosted API is coming up at the end of the quarter and procurement asked me to line up options for commit sizing and overage treatment. Usage has grown faster than we modeled in Q1 (see attached usage-report-q1.csv).

Top asks:
- We want a proposal that lets us avoid big surprises if burst usage continues — flexible buffer credits or an authorized overage band would help.
- Prefer per-token pricing continuity but open to a step-discount path as we hit volumes.
- Need to understand renewal uplift limits / how much our committed token baseline can change year-over-year without extensive renegotiation.

Can you send two options: 1) conservative commit + small buffer credits, and 2) a more aggressive discount/step plan if we commit to a larger floor? Procurement also needs a sample invoice and a SOC2 addendum.

Thanks — can we get something by next Wednesday?

Best,
Emily
Head of Platform, Acme Analytics

Attachment: usage-report-q1.csv (CSV)
From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Fri, 9 Apr 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Renewal planning — right-sizing + overage / buffer options

Emily — thanks for the context and the report. Very helpful.

I’m attaching a concise termsheet with two structured options aligned to your asks:
1) Flexible Buffer Option — conservative commit (baseline = 60% of trailing 90d peak) + 15% credits buffer each month; overage beyond buffer charged at standard per-token rate; quarterly true-up.
2) Step-Discount Path — commit bands with automatic per-token discounts at breakpoints (see table in spreadsheet). Example: 0–250M tokens = list price; 250–750M = 12% off; 750–1.5B = 20% off; 1.5B+ = 28% off. We can include a 12-month uplift cap of 25% on the commit baseline to limit year-over-year movement without escalation.

Key notes:
- We recommend the Flexible Buffer if you expect bursty traffic but want predictable unit economics.
- The Step-Discount Path drives stronger economics in exchange for higher committed floors.
- We can offer a one-quarter soft-commit pilot (soft true-up with credits rather than cash) to reduce upfront friction.

Next steps: internal review on your side, then a 30–45 minute pricing call to lock the banding and finalize DocuSign terms. I’ve attached the termsheet and a short PDF that shows the discount step math.

If procurement needs a sample invoice and SOC2 addendum, I’ll loop in our finance and compliance folks after you confirm which option you prefer.

Cheers,
Soojin Lee
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
soojin.lee@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0189

Attachment: ACME_Renewal_Termsheet_v3.xlsx (XLSX)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 10 Apr 2027 10:30:00 -0700
Subject: internal: margin check + recommended floors for ACME

Soojin / Lauren — quick internal note before we finalize the termsheet we send:
- Acme’s trailing 90d tokenize is ~420M (see Emily’s attachment). If we set a conservative baseline at 60% we’re at ~250M tokens commit — reasonable starter.
- Margin sensitivity: step discounts of 12%/20%/28% (as proposed) look OK if we require minimum commit durations and include a usage true-up. The 28% band requires a firm 12-month commit and a 90% floor (i.e., they must commit to at least 90% of the tier expected usage).
- Recommend we add a clause: if they exceed the uplift cap of 25% in year 1, any extra volume above 25% moves to a higher-priced band for the remainder of the year (protects unit economics).
- For SOC2/addendum and sample invoice, finance will provide redacted invoice + compliance matrix. I’ll draft the invoice stub.

If we want to push for Dedicated pricing, we can model that but ACME currently benefits from Hosted simplicity — keep that as an optional appendix only.

Karthik
Director, Sales Strategy

Date: Sun, 11 Apr 2027 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: internal: margin check + recommended floors for ACME

+1 to Karthik’s point. Couple of pragmatic guardrails I want in the customer-facing sheet:
- Cap discount depth at 30% absolute (beyond that we require a co-signed commercial exec approval).
- Make the soft-commit pilot explicit: 90-day soft true-up where buffer credits offset overages — only cash true-ups at the end of pilot if they elected hard commit.
- Add a short clause on rollback: if monthly average usage drops below 50% of baseline for two consecutive months, we reserve the right to reprice new overages (protects us from sustained under-utilization).

Also, share the draft DocuSign link once the termsheet is updated so procurement can review the legal language.

Lauren
Sr. Director, Enterprise Sales Operations

Thanks Soojin — helpful framing and the two options look workable. A couple of follow-ups from procurement: 
- We prefer the Flexible Buffer plus the 90-day soft-commit pilot to avoid immediate capital commitment. If the pilot achieves the forecasted uplift, we’d convert to the Step-Discount Path at the agreed floor.
- For the Step-Discount path, our finance team asked if you can move the first breakpoint to 200M (from 250M) and make the first step 10% (instead of 12%) — they need a softer entry to show immediate savings.
- Procurement also requires a sample invoice and SOC2 addendum before legal signs.

We can do the 30–45 minute call on Wednesday (their time) — can you send a calendar invite? If you can include a draft DocuSign link and the updated termsheet, procurement will fast-track it.

Appreciate the flexibility — looking forward to wrapping this up.

Best,
Emily
